steps.title: Cold stratify seeds
steps.instruction: Place approximately four times the required number of Arabidopsis seeds into a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube, add 500–1,000 µL ultrapure water, cover with aluminum foil, and refrigerate at 4 °C for 2–4 days.

steps.title: Sow seeds and grow plants
steps.instruction: Mix potting soil and fine‑grain vermiculite 1:1, fill each cell of a 25‑well plastic cell tray with the mixture, place the tray into a plastic tray, water the soil surface with tap water (≈10 passes until fully moist) and discard outflow, sow ~4 stratified seeds per cell using a 200 µL micropipette with a wide‑bore tip, cover the tray with plastic wrap, and incubate in a growth chamber at 23 °C, 12 h light/12 h dark, 90–130 µmol·m⁻²·s⁻¹ photon flux density. Remove the wrap 2–4 days after sowing when most seeds have germinated, thin to 1–2 plants per cell ~14 days after sowing, and grow for a total of 20–24 days. Water with tap water twice weekly and add Hyponex solution (1:2,000 dilution) to the tap water once weekly.

steps.title: Add MES buffer to plate
steps.instruction: Add 1 mL of 10 mM MES‑NaOH (pH 5.5) buffer to each well of a 12‑well cell‑culture plate.

steps.title: Excise and infiltrate leaf
steps.instruction: At the end of a 12‑h dark period, excise the second rosette leaf with stainless‑steel scissors, place it on a fingertip using tweezers, flip it to expose the abaxial surface, remove air from a 1‑mL syringe by drawing and ejecting MES buffer 3–4 times, then draw ~300 µL MES buffer, gently press the syringe tip onto the abaxial surface and infiltrate <10 µL of buffer with moderate pressure, and transfer the infiltrated leaf into a well of the plate.

steps.title: Incubate infiltrated leaves in dark
steps.instruction: Place the plate in a temperature‑controlled incubator at 23 °C with the lid slightly open for ventilation, and incubate in darkness for 5–8 hours to induce sugar starvation and autophagy.

steps.title: Prepare leaf fragment for microscopy
steps.instruction: Immediately before observation, excise the outer edge of the pretreated leaf with scissors, place the resulting fragment into a glass‑bottom dish so the adaxial surface contacts the glass, add ~200 µL MES buffer around the fragment, gently place a round cover glass on top (buffer should pull the glass down to seal, avoiding bubbles), and mount the dish on the stage of an inverted confocal microscope.

steps.title: Set confocal microscope parameters
steps.instruction: Use an inverted Zeiss LSM 900 (or equivalent). Set excitation/detection as follows: GFP – 488 nm excitation, 410–546 nm (or 550 nm) detection; RFP – 561 nm excitation, 550–640 nm detection; Chlorophyll – 488 nm or 640 nm excitation, 656–700 nm detection. Adjust laser power according to fluorophore (e.g., 0.8% for 488 nm GFP, 1.0% for 561 nm RFP, 1.0% for 640 nm chlorophyll) and follow the specific settings listed in Table 1 of the protocol.

steps.title: Capture fluorescence images
steps.instruction: Acquire fluorescence signals for each marker (GFP, RFP, chlorophyll) using the settings above. For multi‑color samples, detect GFP and chlorophyll simultaneously on one track and RFP on a second track, switching tracks every line in the ZEN software to minimize crosstalk.

steps.title: Perform time‑lapse imaging (optional)
steps.instruction: To monitor chloroplast budding, locate the GFP‑ATG8a‑labeled isolation membrane in a wide‑field scan, narrow the scan area to magnify the membrane, and start time‑lapse acquisition using the ZEN Time Series function. Use sequential detection tracks as described, and record images (e.g., every 2 s) for later analysis.

description: Validation of protocol Structures similar to those shown in Figures 2 and 3 , as well as Video 1 , were observed in leaves from 2–3 independent plants.
